title: What signs indicate that Python's dataclasses are NOT a good fit for a particular use-case?
q_body: I find Python's dataclasses to be incredibly convenient. They cut out a ton of boilerplate code (no more needing to write self.foo = foo for every __init__ parameter, and no more needing to spell out attribute after attribute in the rich-comparison methods) They cut out code maintenance when a new attribute is added to a class (the automatic __eq__ , __repr__ , etc. will all automatically incorporate the new field) They make it easy to inspect classes or their instances ( dataclasses.fields , dataclasses.asdict , etc.) It's easy to pick-and-choose functionality; if you need something more specific than its default __eq__ , just write it yourself and the @dataclasses.dataclass decorator incorporates it seamlessly They're so good, in fact, that I find myself using them all over the place for new code, and looking at some of my old existing code and wondering if there's any reason I shouldn't refactor any "manual" classes into dataclasses instead. Even when a class isn't much of a "data class" (maybe it's only got one or two __init__ parameters, for example), setting it up as a dataclass still means I don't need to type out the __init__ myself, the boilerplate __init__ completely goes away instead of cluttering the code, and I get all of the other dataclass benefits for free. So... why not? What are some red flags that using a dataclass is not a good idea? title: Unity: ML-Agents training freeze with RenderTexture on Unity 6.3 LTS and ML-Agents 4.0.2 (eventually resumes)
q_body: I am training a PPO agent using ML-Agents 4.0.2 on Unity 6.3 LTS and I am encountering a reproducible long-running stall that appears to be related to visual observations via RenderTexture. The setup runs multiple parallel environments and uses a RenderTexture-based visual observation. Training behaves normally for roughly 20 to 60 minutes. At some point, the simulation stops progressing. Academy.StepCount no longer increases and the Python trainer waits indefinitely for new data. The Unity processes remain alive and do not crash, and there are no clear exceptions in the logs. System resources (CPU, GPU, memory) appear stable at the time of the stall. After another 20–30 minutes of inactivity, training suddenly resumes and continues as if nothing happened. This makes it look less like a crash and more like some kind of internal blocking or deadlock that eventually clears. I verified that the issue is independent of whether the trainer runs on GPU or CPU. Lowering the Unity quality level does not change the behavior either. I added a watchdog on the Unity side to confirm that Academy.StepCount truly stops advancing during the stall. The most important observation is this: when I remove the RenderTexture observation entirely and switch to non-visual observations, the problem no longer occurs. With the same training configuration but without RenderTexture-based sensors, training runs continuously without freezing. At this point it appears that the Unity simulation loop is being blocked somewhere in the visual observation pipeline rather than the Python trainer crashing. Versio
